Quick update from runtime side:
- KV cache eviction spike confirmed between 08:18–08:35 UTC for the model family rivermark-core-v2; TTLs showed unexpected expirations due to a partial cache invalidation triggered by a housekeeping job that ran across AZ2 racks at 08:17.
- We captured a KVCACHE dump (attached) and sampled traces show cache-miss amplification causing more calls to the hot path which increases p99 latencies.

Mitigation options:
A) Warm caches from snapshot + surgical restart of the housekeeping job on affected racks (low blast, expected recovery 10–15m).
B) Cross-region reroute for Rivermark to eastus2/USW2 while we heal AZ2 (higher latency for some users but keeps throughput).

I recommend A + selective prefix-level reroute for ~10% of traffic (canary) to validate reroute safety.

Aditya
Senior Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident wrap & exec note — EastUS AZ2 (P1)

Jessica / Rivermark team — thank you for raising this quickly and for patience while we worked the command post. Short summary for execs:
- Root cause: partial network fabric packet loss on a subset of AZ2 racks triggered a housekeeping job to drop keys; this created a cache-miss amplification for rivermark-core-v2 and increased runtime p99s and 5xxs.
- Mitigations taken: disabled the housekeeping job for AZ2, applied cache warm snapshots to affected machines, and drained two affected racks from traffic while AWS investigates fabric errors.
- User impact: 08:20–09:05 UTC, approx 45 minutes of elevated errors and throughput reduction for ~8% of global requests tied to the account's traffic distribution.
- Next steps: we will run a post-incident review, push a hardening change to prevent cross-rack invalidations, and prepare an SLA reconciliation for Rivermark.

We've scheduled an exec sync at 17:30 PST to review follow-ups; Marissa will share the post-incident slide and a proposed credit package.

Apologies for the outage. Please reach out if you'd like more detail.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
